fields.label_en: Commitment to contribute to a circular economy
fields.description: Organization seeks to understand and commit or contribute to a circular economy while contributing to sustainable development.
fields.verification_quote: It is applicable to organizations seeking to understand and commit or contribute to a circular economy while contributing to sustainable development. — printed p.1 (§1) = PDF p.8

fields.description: Jurisdiction in which the organization is located.
fields.verification_quote: These organizations can be either private or public, acting individually or collectively, regardless of type or size, and located in any jurisdiction, or position within a specific value chain or value network. — printed p.1 (§1) = PDF p.8

fields.description: Identity of the organization seeking to commit/contribute to a circular economy.
Private or public; individual or collective; regardless of type or size.
fields.verification_quote: These organizations can be either private or public, acting individually or collectively, regardless of type or size, and located in any jurisdiction, or position within a specific value chain or value network. — printed p.1 (§1) = PDF p.8

fields.label_en: Position within the value chain or value network
fields.description: Where the organization's solutions fit in the value chain/network; prerequisite before implementing actions (6.1).
fields.verification_quote: Prior to implementing any of the identified actions in this clause, an organization should have an understanding of where their solutions fit in the value chain. | These organizations can be either private or public, acting individually or collectively, regardless of type or size, and located in any jurisdiction, or position within a specific value chain or value network. — printed p.18 (§6.1) and p.1 (§1) = PDF p.25 and p.8

fields.description: Element of an organization's activities/solutions that interacts with the circular economy (durability, recyclability, reusability, repairability, recoverability).
fields.verification_quote: circularity aspect | element of an organization’s (3.4.1) activities or solutions (3.2.1) that interacts with the circular economy (3.1.1) | EXAMPLE Durability, recyclability, reusability, repairability, recoverability. — printed p.13 (§3.6.1) = PDF p.20

fields.description: Selector over the 23 circular-economy terms (3.1); supportive vocabulary lookup.
fields.verification_quote: 3.1 Terms related to a circular economy | circular economy | economic system (3.1.2) that uses a systemic approach to maintain a circular flow of resources (3.1.6), by recovering, retaining or adding to their value (3.1.7), while contributing to sustainable development (3.1.11) | system in focus | system (3.1.22) that is defined by selected system boundaries and is the subject of a circularity measurement (3.6.4) and a circularity assessment (3.6.5) — printed pp.1-4 (§3.1.1 and §3.1.23) = PDF pp.8-11

fields.description: System defined by selected boundaries, subject of a circularity measurement/assessment (regional, interorganizational, organizational, product).
fields.verification_quote: system in focus | system (3.1.22) that is defined by selected system boundaries and is the subject of a circularity measurement (3.6.4) and a circularity assessment (3.6.5) | Note 1 to entry: Four system levels are being used for measuring and assessing circularity performance (3.6.3): regional, interorganizational, organizational and product level. — printed p.4 (§3.1.23) = PDF p.11

fields.description: Long-term vision: reduced, efficient, effective use of resources and prevention of harmful releases/losses/degradation when meeting societal needs; decoupling growth from resource consumption.
fields.verification_quote: The long-term vision of a circular economy is, by design, to provide appropriate solutions for the reduced, efficient and effective use of resources, and to prevent harmful releases, losses and environmental degradation when meeting societal needs. | Under this vision, social and economic growth are decoupled from resource consumption. — printed pp.14-15 (§4) = PDF pp.21-22

fields.description: The six principles (Clause 5) should be integrated into organizational strategies and objectives.
fields.verification_quote: The six principles described in Clause 5 should be integrated into organizational strategies and objectives to support continual progress towards increasing circularity. — printed p.15 (§4) = PDF p.22

fields.description: Systems thinking should be applied to circular economy activities (Clause 4 / 5.2.1).
fields.verification_quote: Systems thinking should be applied to circular economy activities, which supports progress towards sustainable development. — printed p.15 (§4) = PDF p.22

fields.description: Focusing on only one or two principles can undermine achievements; integrating all six is important (5.3.2).
fields.verification_quote: Considering the integration of all the circular economy principles is important, as focusing on only one or two principles can undermine the achievements that would otherwise occur if all the principles were considered. — printed p.16 (§5.3.2) = PDF p.23

fields.description: A risk-based approach should be used to avoid exposure to hazardous substances; where possible organizations should avoid their use.
fields.verification_quote: A circular economy should not harm the health of people, wildlife or the environment. Therefore, a risk-based approach should be used to avoid exposure to hazardous substances. When possible, organizations should avoid their use. — printed p.17 (§5.3.4) = PDF p.24

fields.description: One of the six interlinked principles considered for the transition; all should be considered together.
fields.verification_quote: The set of principles given in 5.2, which are interlinked and complementary, should be considered by an organization to transition towards a circular economy. | 5.2.1 Systems thinking | 5.2.2 Value creation | 5.2.3 Value sharing | 5.2.4 Resource stewardship | 5.2.5 Resource traceability | 5.2.6 Ecosystem resilience — printed pp.15-16 (§5.1 and §5.2) = PDF pp.22-23

fields.description: Organization identifies and measures use of all resource types and traces mass and value over time; monitors losses by type, disposition and effects.
fields.verification_quote: To efficiently manage the resource utilization in a circular way, the organization can identify and measure the use of all types of resources (virgin or recovered, non-renewable or renewable) and trace the mass and value over time, while resource substitution, resource recovery and recycling are carried out and improved. There is inevitably loss of resources (e.g. material and energy) over time that should be monitored in terms of type, final disposition and effects. — printed p.17 (§5.3.6) = PDF p.24

fields.description: Grouping of actions: added value, value retention, value recovery, ecosystem regeneration, transition support.
fields.verification_quote: 6.2 Actions that create added value | 6.3 Actions that contribute to value retention | 6.4 Actions that contribute to value recovery | 6.5 Actions to regenerate ecosystems | 6.6 Actions to support a circular economy transition — printed pp.18, 21, 22, 25 (§6.2 to §6.6) = PDF pp.25, 28, 29, 32

fields.description: A life cycle perspective should guide the identification of the best action for the value creation model and to avoid unwanted trade-offs.
fields.verification_quote: This resource management guidance is intended to help organizations prioritize actions to increase circularity performance. A life cycle perspective should guide the organization in the identification of the best action for their value creation model and to avoid unwanted trade-offs. — printed p.27 (§6.7) = PDF p.34

fields.description: Organizations should consider refuse and rethink as preliminary actions.
fields.verification_quote: Organizations should consider refuse and rethink as preliminary actions. — printed p.18 (§6.1) = PDF p.25

fields.description: In general, products should be repaired before remanufactured, and remanufactured before recycled - unless a life cycle perspective yields a better outcome.
fields.verification_quote: In general, products should be repaired before they are remanufactured, and remanufactured before they are recycled. However, in cases where applying this guidance does not lead to the best outcome, organizations should consider applying a life cycle perspective to determine the best action. — printed p.28 (§6.7) = PDF p.35

fields.description: Action chosen from the R-strategy hierarchy (refuse->re-mine), prioritized via a life cycle perspective.
fields.verification_quote: The guidance (see Table 1) suggests organizations can begin by determining if there is a need to be satisfied and if the need can be met without additional resource use (refuse). [...] designing solutions that use fewer resources (rethink, reduce) and prioritizing the use of recovered resources [...] (source). | Organizations should seek to extend the life of solutions by design and by maintaining the solution in use for as long as possible (repair, reuse, refurbish, remanufacture, repurpose) while continuing to provide value. | Finally, organizations should look to use resources in multiple cycles (cascade, recycle), recover the energy if the resource cannot be used again (energy recovery) or source resources from landfills (re-mine). — pp.27-28 (§6.7, Tab. 1) = PDF pp.34-35

fields.description: Selected circularity indicators should be calculated and a baseline circularity assessment performed (methods owned by ISO 59020).
fields.verification_quote: As part of the reference situation assessment, the selected circularity indicators should be calculated and a baseline circularity assessment performed. A baseline can assist the organization when setting targets for a circular transition, assessing progress, evaluating the effectiveness of actions introduced, and making improvements, as needed. | NOTE 2 More information on how to identify appropriate circularity indicators can be found in ISO 59020. — printed p.31 (§7.2.2) = PDF p.38

fields.description: Action plan for how the strategy will be implemented; scope, responsibilities, capabilities, timeline, potential setbacks.
fields.verification_quote: Once the circular economy strategic priorities are established, the organization should develop an action plan for how the circular economy strategy will be implemented. This should include consideration of the scope and capabilities for the circular economy implementation. | The organization should determine responsibilities for the different steps and critical areas towards circularity. | The action plan for a circular economy also should consider the capabilities allocated and timeline for implementation and should identify potential setbacks that can occur during the implementation phase, so that preventive measures, if necessary, can be adopted. — printed pp.34-35 (§7.4.6) = PDF pp.41-42

fields.description: Goals with intermediate targets to allow circularity assessments of progress from the reference situation towards longer-term goals.
fields.verification_quote: The organization should develop goals with an aim to create structured and lasting change and identify pathways and key actions to achieve their vision for a circular economy. Intermediate targets should be established to allow for circularity assessments of progress from the reference situation towards the longer-term goals. — printed p.33 (§7.3.2) = PDF p.40

fields.label_en: Circular economy purpose, mission and vision
fields.description: Purpose, mission and vision developed in alignment with the circular economy principles; should inspire change and provide clear direction.
fields.verification_quote: Organizations should develop their purpose, mission and vision for a circular economy in alignment with the circular economy principles (see 5.2). The vision should inspire change and provide a clear direction for the organization to transition towards a circular economy. — printed p.32 (§7.3.1) = PDF p.39

fields.description: Strategy linking mission, vision, goals, priorities, targets and respective actions/projects followed by a measuring framework and a set of circularity indicators.
fields.verification_quote: An organization’s strategy should link its mission, vision, goals, priorities, targets and respective actions or projects followed by a measuring framework. This should also include the establishment of a set of circularity indicators that allows for monitoring the strategic priorities and action plan implementation and goals achievement, as well as the outcomes of the different actions applied (see ISO 59020). — printed p.33 (§7.4.3) = PDF p.40

fields.description: Dimension against which actions are assessed for feasibility: technical, organizational, financial/economic, context, social, environmental.
fields.verification_quote: To assess the feasibility of the adoption of a circular economy and its associated circular economy value creation models, actions should be assessed against the following dimensions: | technical aspects [...] | organizational aspects [...] | financial and economic aspects: financial feasibility for the organization [...] | context aspects: regulatory frameworks, institutional settings and social norms [...] | social aspects: the impact on social systems, including the social equity benefits to be achieved; | environmental aspects: the environmental impacts considering the different scenarios where actions will be implemented. — printed p.34 (§7.4.5) = PDF p.41

fields.description: System level at which the organization operates: global/regional/country/local, interorganizational, organizational (product covered indirectly).
fields.verification_quote: This guidance is applicable to organizations operating at all system levels, as follows: | Global, regional, country, local level: covers, but is not limited to, international agencies, countries, states, provinces, cities and municipalities. | Interorganizational level: covers inter-industry and inter-firm networks [...] | Organizational level: covers any type of organization [...] | ISO 59020 covers these three levels and also includes a system level focusing on products. This fourth system level is indirectly covered in this document by the goals, strategies and activities of the organizations that provide products. — printed p.29 (§7.1.3) = PDF p.36

fields.description: Stage of the iterative implementation process (Figure 4): context assessment, purpose/goals, strategy/action plan, implementation, monitoring.
fields.verification_quote: The guidance is structured to allow for an iterative process. The stages of implementation can be altered and adapted to reflect changing circumstances of the organization. Figure 4 illustrates the stages, which are underpinned by the circular economy principles. | The proposed stages that an organization can undertake in order to implement a circular economy are discussed in 7.2 to 7.6. | NOTE The sequence of stages can differ and can also occur at the same time or in parallel. — printed p.30 (§7.1.4, Figure 4) = PDF p.37

fields.description: Organization should choose circularity indicators and often review indicators and circularity performance to set the basis for continual improvement.
fields.verification_quote: The organization should often review these indicators and circularity performance. The review links the actions to the circular economy principles. | Review of the circularity indicators and circularity performance should set the basis for continual improvement and, therefore, can include milestones and targets for the next period. — printed p.36 (§7.6) = PDF p.43

fields.description: Preliminary pilot application of a specific practice/segment to ensure it works as planned and risks/barriers are addressed before wider implementation.
fields.verification_quote: Prior to formal implementation some organizations can consider a preliminary pilot application of a specific circular economy practice or for a specific segment of the organization to ensure the application works as planned and any specific risk or barriers are addressed before wider implementation. — printed p.35 (§7.4.7) = PDF p.42

fields.description: Organization should determine its reference situation regarding a circular economy (current practices, resource flows, alignment with principles).
fields.verification_quote: As an initial step, the organization should determine their reference situation with regards to a circular economy. This may encompass, but is not limited to: | identifying current resource management practices in the organization and its value chain(s) or value network(s); | assessing the flow of resources used by the organization; | assessing the current organizational practices and understanding how they align with the circular economy principles; — printed p.31 (§7.2.2) = PDF p.38

fields.description: Indicator chosen to assess effectiveness/efficiency of interventions and monitor progress; determined with the principles, goals and strategic priorities in mind.
fields.verification_quote: As part of its action plan for a circular economy (see 7.1.4), the organization should choose circularity indicators to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of the interventions adopted and monitor the progress. The circularity indicators should be determined with the circular economy principles in mind, as well as the circularity goals and strategic priorities established by the organization. — printed p.36 (§7.6) = PDF p.43

fields.description: Value creation model aligned with the circular economy; explored to address identified opportunities to create value.
fields.verification_quote: The organization should align its actions with the strategy and address identified opportunities to create value and have a value creation model in place that is aligned with the circular economy. — printed p.33 (§7.4.4) = PDF p.40

requirements.condition: organization_name IS NOT NULL AND organization_type IS NOT NULL AND value_chain_position IS NOT NULL
requirements.description: The organization seeking to understand and commit or contribute to a circular economy while contributing to sustainable development is identified, with its type, jurisdiction and value-chain position.

requirements.title_de: Commitment to a circular economy declared
requirements.title_en: Commitment to a circular economy declared
requirements.description: Organization commits or contributes to a circular economy while contributing to sustainable development.
The long-term vision (reduced/efficient/effective resource use; prevention of harmful releases, losses and degradation; decoupling growth from resource consumption) is established.
Systems thinking should be applied to circular economy activities to support progress towards sustainable development.
The six principles described in Clause 5 should be integrated into organizational strategies and objectives to support continual progress towards increasing circularity.
Organizations take a life cycle perspective and apply a long-term approach when considering their impacts on environmental, social and economic systems.
Organizations recover, retain or add value by providing effective solutions that contribute to socio-economic and environmental value, and use resources in an efficient way.
Organizations collaborate with interested parties along the value chain or value network in an inclusive and equitable way, sharing the value created with the provision of a solution.
Organizations manage stocks and flows in a sustainable way including by closing, slowing and narrowing resource flows, to reduce risks associated with dependence on virgin resources.
Organizations collect and maintain data to enable tracking of resources through their value chains and are accountable for sharing relevant information with interested parties.

Organizations develop and implement practices and strategies that protect and contribute to the resilience and regeneration of ecosystems and their biodiversity, incl. preventing harmful losses and releases and taking into account planetary boundaries.

Circular economy principles should be considered in the early stages of design and development of a solution to create the highest possible value relative to resource use and minimize waste, losses and releases.

requirements.title_de: Integrate all principles, not one or two
requirements.title_en: Integrate all principles, not one or two
requirements.description: Considering the integration of all the circular economy principles is important, as focusing on only one or two can undermine achievements.

requirements.title_de: Collaborate for management of information and resources
requirements.title_en: Collaborate for management of information and resources
requirements.description: Organizations should collaborate to improve transparency when monitoring resource stocks and flows on an ongoing basis and identify opportunities to add/retain/recover value and track/manage resources.

A circular economy should not harm health of people, wildlife or the environment; a risk-based approach should be used to avoid exposure to hazardous substances and, where possible, avoid their use. [BLOCK-EXCEPTION: safety — §5.3.4 — ignoring the risk-based approach to hazardous substances plausibly causes physical harm to the health of people and wildlife]
requirements.source_quote: A circular economy should not harm the health of people, wildlife or the environment. Therefore, a risk-based approach should be used to avoid exposure to hazardous substances. When possible, organizations should avoid their use.

requirements.title_de: Optimize value creation relative to resource use
requirements.title_en: Optimize value creation relative to resource use
requirements.description: Organizations should consider what approach is optimal in relation to provided value and resource use, considering not only resources used in solutions but the full effects of the supporting system.
Organizations should understand stocks and flows relevant to their solutions/activities, identify and measure use of all resource types, trace mass and value over time, and monitor losses.

requirements.title_de: Consider refuse and rethink as preliminary actions
requirements.title_en: Consider refuse and rethink as preliminary actions
requirements.description: Prior to implementing actions, organizations should understand where their solutions fit in the value chain and should consider refuse and rethink as preliminary actions.

requirements.title_de: Prioritize resource stewardship in added-value actions
requirements.title_en: Prioritize resource stewardship in added-value actions
requirements.description: Organizations should rethink solutions especially at design stage and, as a priority, consider the principle of resource stewardship to enable circulation and prevent waste and harmful losses and releases.

Design for circularity should rethink solutions so they can be repaired/maintained/refurbished/remanufactured/upgraded/reused, minimize resource use and prolong product lifetime, integrating all CE principles.
When implementing circular sourcing, organizations should minimize resource use and give preference to acquiring recovered and renewable resources while taking into account life cycle impacts.
Organizations should invest in activities (reuse, leasing, sharing, maintaining, refurbishing, remanufacturing) to retain the value of resources, considered from the design stage.
Organizations should implement product collection, sorting and recovery efficiently and review actions for resource management to select the most appropriate and viable actions.

requirements.title_de: Energy recovery only as circular when life-cycle optimal
requirements.title_en: Energy recovery only as circular when life-cycle optimal
requirements.description: Energy recovery efforts deployed without considering a material's place in the circular flow and the broader environmental impact are not considered circular; energy recovery should be optimized.

To align with ecosystem resilience, regeneration of degraded ecosystems can encompass removal of harmful substances, remediation of soil/water, climate mitigation/adaptation and biodiversity protection.

requirements.title_de: Actions to support a circular economy transition
requirements.title_en: Actions to support a circular economy transition
requirements.description: Relevant actors should participate to enable a systems change; subsystems (education, research, political, legal, economic, financial) should be reformed and support provided for the evolution of cultural values.

requirements.title_de: Apply resource-management guidance via life cycle perspective
requirements.title_en: Apply resource-management guidance via life cycle perspective
requirements.description: Organizations should use the R-strategy guidance (Table 1) and apply a life cycle perspective to identify the best action for their value creation model and avoid unwanted trade-offs.
In general, products should be repaired before they are remanufactured, and remanufactured before recycled, unless a life cycle perspective indicates a better outcome.

requirements.title_de: Implementation process based on CE understanding
requirements.title_en: Implementation process based on CE understanding
requirements.description: The implementation process should be based on an understanding of the circular economy, its principles, and how it can be adapted to the specific needs of the organization and its context.

requirements.title_de: Incorporate principles in each implementation stage
requirements.title_en: Incorporate principles in each implementation stage
requirements.description: The implementation process should consider the principles; steps in each stage should be aligned with the principles, considered before deciding on a specific strategy.
The guidance applies at all system levels; organizations operating across more than one level should consider the relationships and interactions within and between system levels.

requirements.title_de: Assess reference situation and perform baseline assessment
requirements.title_en: Assess reference situation and perform baseline assessment
requirements.description: The organization should determine its reference situation; selected circularity indicators should be calculated and a baseline circularity assessment performed.
Based on the reference situation, the organization should identify and analyse potential risks and key areas of opportunity of a circular economy.

requirements.title_de: Define purpose, mission and vision aligned with principles
requirements.title_en: Define purpose, mission and vision aligned with principles
requirements.description: Organizations should develop their purpose, mission and vision for a circular economy in alignment with the principles; the vision should inspire change and provide clear direction.
The organization should develop goals with intermediate targets to allow circularity assessments of progress from the reference situation towards longer-term goals.
The strategy should link mission, vision, goals, priorities, targets and actions, include a measuring framework and a set of circularity indicators, and address all principles.

requirements.title_de: Explore an aligned value creation model
requirements.title_en: Explore an aligned value creation model
requirements.description: The organization should have a value creation model in place that is aligned with the circular economy and addresses identified opportunities to create value.
Actions should be assessed for feasibility against technical, organizational, financial/economic, context, social and environmental dimensions, in linkage with the context evaluation.
The organization should develop an action plan for how the strategy will be implemented, incl. scope, responsibilities, capabilities, timeline and potential setbacks.
To achieve successful implementation, cooperation inside and outside the organization should be fostered; capacity for action should be built via coaching, training and skills development.
During implementation the strategic priorities and action plan are put into practice and integrated into the organizational culture and daily practices.

requirements.title_de: Monitor, review and report using circularity indicators
requirements.title_en: Monitor, review and report using circularity indicators
requirements.description: The organization should choose circularity indicators to assess effectiveness/efficiency of interventions, often review indicators and performance, and set the basis for continual improvement.
Methods to measure and assess circularity performance (indicator selection, calculation, system boundaries, baseline) are provided by ISO 59020; this document hands measurement to ISO 59020.

requirements.title_de: Value creation models & networks per ISO 59010
requirements.title_en: Value creation models & networks per ISO 59010
requirements.description: Guidance on circular economy value creation models and value networks (transition of business models) is provided by ISO 59010; this document hands value-creation modelling to ISO 59010.
